title: The Wise Men of Chelm and the Cheeky Fish
summary: Reb Tzadok buys a big fish for Shabbat and stuffs it into his pocket, and the fish swishes its tail and slaps him on the cheek! All of Chelm cries out: a trial! The three wise men set up a special court for the fish and hand down the harshest punishment of all: send it to the river... And what does the fish think of that? A rhyming story based on a folk tale of the Wise Men of Chelm.
pages:
Reb Tzadok came out from prayers, a cane in one hand and a bag in the other,
and bought at the market a big fish, fat and silver and shiny like no other.
He stuffed the fish in his coat pocket, its tail poking out in the air,
and sang, "Shabbat is coming! What a bright, clear day, so fair!"

But the fish in the pocket thought, "It's too crowded! Enough, I say!"
and swished its tail — FLAP! — a slap on the cheek, right away.
Reb Tzadok froze in the middle of the street, his mouth open wide,
and the fish peeked out of the pocket and winked, with no guilt inside.

The news raced through the market and every yard, quick, quick, quick:
"A slap for Reb Tzadok! Never was there such a trick!"
Chutzpah! Chutzpah! all of Chelm cried —
and the fish just laughed: blub-blub-bloo, with a grin so wide!

The three wise men sat in the market like judges in a row,
with long white beards and tall hats, all set for the show.
Reb Shmerel banged his gavel: "The trial is open — and please, no noise!"
And the fish sat on a little chair — with not one bit of fear, all poise.

"Did you slap him?" asked Reb Kalman. And the fish said, "Blub."
"Do you confess?" And the fish said, "Blub, blub, blub!"
And Gitele covered her mouth with both her hands,
but it didn't help — the laughter burst out of her eyes, you understand!

The three wise men whispered, and talked it over, and whispered some more,
till Reb Shmerel stood up: "The verdict — very harsh, that's for sure!
The fish will go to the river, so deep and so cold,
there it will think about what it did — a harder punishment was never told!"

Four strong men carried a bucket, the fish swimming inside,
and all of Chelm marched behind them, slowly, in a line, side by side.
Chutzpah! Chutzpah! all of Chelm cried —
and the fish just laughed: blub-blub-bloo, with a grin so wide!

Reb Shmerel announced, "Now into the water it goes!"
All of Chelm sighed, "Oh, what a punishment!" — and the fish? Its eyes sparkled, as everyone knows.

The four strong men tipped the bucket — and PLOP! the fish dove down,
turned a somersault in the river, waved its fin, and laughed like a pot rolling around.

The wise men scratched their beards and said, "Oh, it's suffering! It's suffering so!"
And the fish leaped out of the water and splashed them — bullseye! — from head to toe!
Chutzpah! Chutzpah! all of Chelm cried —
and the fish just laughed: blub-blub-bloo, with a grin so wide!

Reb Tzadok went home with no fish, and a cheek warm and red,
and on the table waited a challah shaped like a fish — with sesame — and the sweet smell of Shabbat spread.

And in the evening the fish peeked out of the river so wide,
with a green leaf on its head, like a Chelm wise man's hat, worn with pride.
Chutzpah! Chutzpah! all of Chelm cried —
and the fish just laughed: blub-blub-bloo, with a grin so wide!
